title: Investigation of D‐Shape Plastic Optical Fiber Towards Ethanol Concentration
content:
A d-shaped plastic optical fiber (POF) sensor coated with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) was developed for real-time ethanol concentration detection. The d-shaped sensing region enhances evanescent-field interaction with the surrounding ethanol solution, while the CNT coating further improves light–matter interaction and ethanol adsorption. The sensor was evaluated at different ethanol concentrations using a broadband light source and spectrometer. Among the fabricated sensors, the 0.5 mm CNT-coated d-shaped POF achieved the highest sensitivity of 8.94%I/%c, together with good linearity and repeatability. The results demonstrate the potential of the sensor as a low-cost, flexible and practical platform for real-time ethanol monitoring in food, beverage and industrial applications.


ABSTRACT

This research aims to address the challenges of real-time, cost-effective ethanol detection for applications in the food industry by developing a d-shaped plastic optical fiber sensor enhanced with carbon nanotube coatings. Current refractive index sensors often depend on glass optical fibers, which require etching or grating modifications, making them fragile and impractical for real-world applications. Furthermore, many existing sensors demand laboratory-based analysis, resulting in delays and increased costs. In response, this project proposes a robust d-shaped POF sensor as a durable and flexible alternative to glass fibers, leveraging CNT coatings for improved sensitivity through enhanced evanescent field interaction. The project objectives include fabricating d-shaped POFs with diameters of 0.5 and 0.7 mm, applying CNT coatings via a U-groove sanding technique, and conducting sensing experiments for ethanol concentrations ranging from 5% to 25%. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the 0.5 mm CNT-coated POF sensor, which achieved the highest sensitivity of 8.94%I/%c and exhibited strong linearity and repeatability across varying ethanol concentrations. These findings highlight the potential of d-shaped POF sensors in real-time ethanol detection, offering a practical and scalable alternative to existing systems. This study demonstrates the sensing capabilities of CNT-coated d-shaped POF sensors for ethanol detection and highlights their potential for future applications in industrial and biochemical sensing.
